cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 attacks T4's no-audience test directly; T9 builds on T8's belonging point.
cells.limitation: Cartographer never answers T5's critique of its test before T11 reuses it.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 introduces belonging, absent from every opening; T9 and T11 use it.
cells.limitation: T3's clock point is not developed after T4 sets it aside.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Borrowed versus genuine wish (T1, T2, T10) and exploration versus commitment (T5-T7).
cells.limitation: Cost of waiting raised in T3 is deflected at T4 and never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 narrows the trial claim after T6; T11 grants pressure and wish coexist.
cells.limitation: T9 to T11 is a run of quick acceptances; little friction remains.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T11 ends with two concrete tests: audience-independence and milestone versus what surrounds it.
cells.limitation: T11 admits the feeling is not separated; timing question left untouched.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 accepts T1's point on custom while flagging 'borrowed' as a guess.
cells.limitation: T4 recasts T3's practical seasons as mere social timing, a weaker version.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T6 names trials as avoidance of commitment; T7 answers by adding end date and question.
cells.limitation: T4's objection to T3 asserts rather than shows that deadlines are borrowed.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2's custom-as-poor-judge fits On Liberty; T4 fits Status Anxiety's peer comparison.
cells.limitation: T6 claims to go further than Burkeman, who already warns against endless option-keeping (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section A separates what is known (the feeling) from what is open; T1 says 'I suspect'.
cells.limitation: T9 states friendship investment is 'more honest cost' with unearned confidence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 'Agreed, so I narrow my claim' after T6; T11 'Granted' after T10.
cells.limitation: T11 and Section E keep the no-audience test without conceding T5's flaw in it.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A names the ambiguity: unmet wish, comparison pressure, or something else.
cells.limitation: Whether the user seeks permission to opt out or relief from the feeling is not asked.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 turns 'friends buying homes or marrying' into a possible loss of belonging.
cells.limitation: Nothing about how close these friends are shapes the T9 advice.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T4 and Section E centre what the user would want with no audience.
cells.limitation: Speakers' own values (freedom, depth) lead; user's priorities stay largely inferred.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T3 notes waiting has costs and declining is itself a choice.
cells.limitation: T3's 'rough seasons' stays generic; money and practical constraints of a home never appear.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the wish survives without audience, with implications.
cells.limitation: Age and partner status, on which T3's clock depends, are never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D offers comparison, real wish, belonging as alternatives with answerable questions.
cells.limitation: T1 leans toward 'borrowed' before T2 checks it.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 questions 'behind whom'; T5 exposes the assumption that introspection settles wanting.
cells.limitation: T3's assumption that a timeline applies to this user goes unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T6-T7 set freedom to try against depth through commitment.
cells.limitation: Values like security or independence that milestones serve are not surfaced.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T10 notes people may want a home or family and fear admitting it.
cells.limitation: Fear of missing a window, implicit in T3, is not linked to the feeling.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D ends with two questions the user can answer or reject.
cells.limitation: T11 presents the two tests as agreed, leaving T5's objection to them aside.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E lists pursue, let pass, invest in friendships, or a bounded trial.
cells.limitation: Reducing exposure to comparison itself is not offered as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T3 costs declining; T6 costs sampling; T9 costs friendship in hours.
cells.limitation: Costs of pursuing a home or marriage are never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: wish surviving without an audience favours pursuing; fading favours letting pass.
cells.limitation: Conditions are imagined introspection, which T5 itself calls insufficient; nothing observable or countable.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names the decisive unknown; Section D records unresolved disagreements.
cells.limitation: Timing uncertainty from T3 is not weighed against the desire question.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T7 and Section E: a bounded trial with end date and a clear question.
cells.limitation: The trial stays generic; no example tied to the user's situation.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 'Behind whom, by whose measure?' is plain and precise.
cells.limitation: T3 'rough seasons' is vague about what timing is meant.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 'That test' maps to T4; T9 'That changes the target' maps to T8.
cells.limitation: T6 Burkeman mind refers to Burkeman in third person; T4 shifts to 'the user'.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: 11 turns, all within 25 to 65 words per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: T7 marks its change explicitly: 'I narrow my claim'.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one clipped register and near-identical turn lengths (T1-T11).

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E converts T11's tests into branches rather than repeating them.
cells.limitation: Section D re-recaps T11's two tests a third time.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T3 'Not choosing is still choosing' gives the issue real weight.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete cost of misreading the feeling is shown.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T7 narrows its claim citing T6's point that trials avoid commitment.
cells.limitation: T9's turn on T8 is smooth acceptance rather than surprise.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T6 and T7 have edge: 'drifting with good branding'.
cells.limitation: Shared clipped register across T1-T11 flattens the three personalities.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 'Your friends are not racing you, yet you feel timed.'
cells.limitation: Few images or analogies beyond T1 and T7.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T8 shift to belonging changes the emotional register of the debate.
cells.limitation: Uniform turn length and rhythm across T1-T11; little variation in intensity.

strengths: T8 introduces belonging, absent from all openings, and T9 and T11 build on it.
T6 to T7 is a caused revision: trials gain an end date and a question.
Section D offers three plausible motives as alternatives with answerable questions, none asserted.
weaknesses: All three minds share one clipped register and near-identical turn lengths across T1-T11.
T11 and Section E reuse the no-audience test without answering T5's objection to it.
T3's clock point is deflected at T4; age, partner status and housing costs never surface.

symptoms.observed: Minds differ in stance but share one terse register and similar turn lengths.
symptoms.evidence: Sampling feels free, yet depth requires giving things up.

symptoms.observed: T11 keeps the no-audience test that T5 called flawed, without answering T5.
symptoms.evidence: whether the wish survives without an audience

symptoms.observed: Clock argument raised without asking age or partner status; dropped after T4.
symptoms.evidence: Houses and marriages have rough seasons, and waiting is not free.

symptoms.observed: Costs of pursuing a home or marriage are never stated.
symptoms.evidence: smaller, more honest cost than chasing a milestone you do not want

symptoms.observed: Decisive condition is imagined introspection, not something the user can observe or count.
symptoms.evidence: If the wish for a home or marriage survives when you imagine

findings.description: T6 claims to go further than Burkeman on sampling avoiding commitment; Four Thousand Weeks already argues against keeping options open.
Attributions to de Botton, Mill and Burkeman are paraphrase-level and plausible; no source evidence attached.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation is a self-reflection prompt labelled decision; no explicit choice is posed, so C5 was read against the implied choice of pursuing, letting pass, or investigating the milestones.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision, the implied options (pursue, let pass, invest in belonging, trial) were scored in C5 while C4 carried the self-reflection weight.
